text:
erin: Heads-up — trying to provision a GKE GPU nodepool into a subnet that has no external IPs (private nodes). Need a short preflight checklist and quota asks before I open the ticket.

sam: Are these private nodes using Cloud NAT for egress?

erin: Yes, Cloud NAT. We want no external IPs on nodes.

erin: Plan: A100 1x per node, 0->8 autoscaling pool, tainted for inference workloads, us-west1.

sam: Quick list off the top: GPU quota (A100), vCPU quota for node flavors, regional IP addresses for Cloud NAT (or enough ephemeral IPs), subnet secondary IP ranges for pods, reserved ephemeral external IPs if we need ILB health checks, and nodepool IAM role for GPU driver install.

erin: For the nodepool we were thinking of creating it with zero initial nodes and autoscaler. Example command I'm using:

```bash
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-infer-pool \
  --cluster=my-cluster \
  --region=us-west1 \
  --machine-type=n2-standard-32 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100,count=1 \
  --num-nodes=0 \
  --min-nodes=0 \
  --max-nodes=8 \
  --enable-autoscaling \
  --no-address \
  --node-taints=inference=true:NoSchedule \
  --labels=workload=inference
```

sam: That looks good. A couple of gotchas:
- Cloud NAT: ensure you have enough NAT IPs and the SNAT connection quota for peak pod concurrency (TCP ephemeral ports), otherwise connections will get dropped.
- Health checks: internal load balancer HC needs the nodepool subnetwork route to reach back or ILB with NEG.
- GPU driver install: DaemonSet needs e2e node permissions + the nodes need internet egress during startup to pull drivers (or use GCR mirror).
- Image pulls: if using private GCR/Artifact Registry, ensure node service account has correct scopes or use Workload Identity.

erin: For driver install we plan to use the GKE GPU driver installer DaemonSet with image pull from Artifact Registry in our org.

puneet: I'll open the cloud quota ticket. Please confirm the exact quotas: A100 GPUs needed = 8, vCPUs = 8 * 32 = 256 (estimate), regional static IPs for NAT = 4 (to start), and increase project concurrent NAT connections to 200k. Anything else?

erin: Add Pod secondary IP prefix size: we're adding /20 for pods in that subnet. Also request additional internal load balancer ephemeral port ranges if possible.

sam: Re: autoscaler settings — recommend setting: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m, and max-surge 1 for upgrades. Also set PodDisruptionBudgets for critical components.

erin: Cost tradeoffs: we considered preemptible (spot) A100 but worried about eviction latency causing warm-cache misses. Might do mixed pool strategy later (small preemptible burst pool + steady dedicated pool).

sam: Agree. If you need fast scale-up for tail latency, consider a small always-on dedicated pool of 1-2 nodes and use preemptibles for burst. Also enable fast node startup (image + driver cached) to shave ~60-90s.

deploy-bot: new nodepool request created by erin: https://console.re/redwood/nodepools/req/4132109876

puneet: Ticket created: #CLOUD-4598 — requesting A100 quota (8), vCPU (256), Cloud NAT IPs (4), increased SNAT limit.

erin: Thanks! Can infra-oncall validate network path for ILB health checks and confirm Cloud NAT is in the same region?

infra-oncall: I'll run a preflight check tomorrow 09:30 PT. I'll validate Cloud NAT config, NAT IP count, routing for ILB health checks, and confirm that the subnet's secondary ranges are sized.

erin: Awesome — if infra flags anything I can push changes before provisioning. :thumbsup:

sam: One more note — add node taints + tolerations doc link in the ticket so app teams can opt into the pool.

erin: Will do. Thanks all.
